name: Safety Perception and Question Framing (Stockholm)
description:
Method replication: same task and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (new Google Street View views of Stockholm, © Google). Kang et al. (2023, Landscape and Urban Planning 236:104768) recruited locals to compare Stockholm street view images on safety, trained a GeoAI model on the votes to map citywide perceived safety, and compared it with a survey of neighbourhood residents. Image-based safety captured instant impressions of the built environment, while resident surveys reflected daily experience; economically vibrant, inner-city streetscapes looked safe but were not always felt as safe by residents, and older adults tended to overestimate their risk of victimisation.

What participants do: after consent, each participant is randomly given one wording, "Which place looks safe?" or "Which place looks less safe?", and compares 10 pairs of Stockholm street views drawn at random from 66. Then neighbourhood of residence, age and gender. The assigned wording is stored as "framing".

Analysis: reverse-code "less safe" answers, then score each image from pairwise wins (e.g. TrueSkill) and compare the two framings; image scores can be joined with segmentation features or neighbourhood statistics as in the paper.

Differences from the original study: (1) the images are 66 new Google Street View views (2016–2026) from random points in central Stockholm, not the paper's image set; (2) the original interface was in Swedish, this template is in English; (3) age and gender questions are additions. The earlier version of this template showed 2 photographs cropped from the paper PDF.
author: Kang, Abraham, Ceccato, Duarte, Gao, Ljungqvist, Zhang, Näsman & Ratti
